title: The effect of multiplying a dimension by a factor of k

sections.title: The effect of multiplying a dimension by a factor of k

subtopics.title: Scaling a rectangular prism
subtopics.exposition: The volume of a rectangular prism with dimensions l, b and h is V = l × b × h = lbh. The surface area of a rectangular prism with dimensions l, b and h is A = 2[(l × h) + (l × b) + (b × h)] = 2(lh + lb + bh). When one dimension of a rectangular prism (the height) is multiplied by 5, the new volume is V1 = l × b × 5h = 5(lbh) = 5V. When one dimension of a rectangular prism (the height) is multiplied by 5, the new surface area is A1 = 2[(l × 5h) + (l × b) + (b × 5h)] = 2(5lh + lb + 5bh). When two dimensions of a rectangular prism (l and h) are multiplied by 5, the new volume is V2 = 5l × b × 5h = 5.5(lbh) = 5^2 × V. When two dimensions of a rectangular prism (l and h) are multiplied by 5, the new surface area is A2 = 2[(5l × 5h) + (5l × b) + (b × 5h)] = 2 × 5(5lh + lb + bh). The new surface area and volume of a prism or cylinder whose dimensions have been multiplied by a constant are calculated by using the surface area and volume formulae from the preceding section. To see the effect of scaling, multiply one, two and then three of the dimensions of the rectangular prism by a constant factor (here 5) and calculate the new volume and surface area each time. To express the new surface area and volume as a factor of the original, first calculate the original volume and surface area, then the new volume and surface area, then compare the new values with the original ones. Step 1: the original volume of the prism with base lengths 3 cm and height 4 cm is V = l × b × h = 3 × 3 × 4 = 36 cm^3. Step 1: the original surface area of the prism is A = 2[(l × h) + (l × b) + (b × h)] = 2[(3 × 4) + (3 × 3) + (3 × 4)] = 66 cm^2. Step 2: multiplying both base lengths by 3 means two of the dimensions are multiplied by a factor of 3. Step 2: the new volume is V_n = 3l × 3b × h = 3(3) × 3(3) × 4 = 324 cm^3. Step 2: the new surface area is A_n = 2[(3l × h) + (3l × 3b) + (3b × h)] = 2[(3(3) × 4) + (3(3) × 3(3)) + (3(3) × 4)] = 306 cm^2. Step 3: to express the new volume as a factor of the original, divide V_n by V: V_n / V = 324 / 36 = 9, so V_n = 9V = 3^2 V. Step 3: to express the new surface area as a factor of the original, divide A_n by A: A_n / A = 306 / 66, so A_n = (306/66)A = (51/11)A. The dimensions of a rectangular prism are written l, b and h. The new surface area is written A_n and the new volume is written V_n.

subtopics.title: Effect of scaling one dimension
subtopics.exposition: When one or more of the dimensions of a prism or cylinder is multiplied by a constant, its surface area and volume change. If the height of a rectangular prism is multiplied by a constant k, then the volume also increases by a factor of k. In this example the volume of a cylinder with radius r and height h is V = πr^2 × h. In this example the surface area of the cylinder is given as A = πr^2 + 2πrh. When the radius of a cylinder is multiplied by k, the new volume is V_n = π(kr)^2 × h = πk^2 r^2 × h = k^2 × πr^2 h = k^2 V. When the radius of a cylinder is multiplied by k, the new surface area is A_n = π(kr)^2 + 2π(kr)h = πk^2 r^2 + 2πkrh = k^2(πr^2) + k(2πrh). To prove the effect of multiplying the height by k, write the new dimensions of the prism as l, b and kh. With the height multiplied by k, the new volume is V_n = l × b × (kh) = k(lbh) = kV. When the radius of the cylinder is multiplied by k, the new dimensions are kr and h.

subtopics.title: Apply scale factor rules
subtopics.exposition: There is a relationship between the change in dimensions and the resulting change in surface area and volume. When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by 5, the new volume is V3 = 5l × 5b × 5h = 5^3(lbh) = 5^3 V. When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by 5, the new surface area is A3 = 2(5^2 lh + 5^2 lb + 5^2 bh) = 5^2 × 2(lh + lb + bh) = 5^2 A. When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by a factor k, the new volume is V_k = kl × kb × kh = k^3(lbh) = k^3 V; volume is multiplied by k^3. When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by a factor k, the new surface area is A_k = 2[(kl × kh) + (kl × kb) + (kb × kh)] = k^2 × 2(lh + lb + bh) = k^2 A; surface area is multiplied by k^2. These relationships are used to calculate the new volume or surface area of an object more simply when its dimensions are scaled up or down.

claims.claim: When one or more of the dimensions of a prism or cylinder is multiplied by a constant, its surface area and volume change.
The new surface area and volume of a prism or cylinder whose dimensions have been multiplied by a constant are calculated by using the surface area and volume formulae from the preceding section.
There is a relationship between the change in dimensions and the resulting change in surface area and volume.
These relationships are used to calculate the new volume or surface area of an object more simply when its dimensions are scaled up or down.
The dimensions of a rectangular prism are written l, b and h.
To see the effect of scaling, multiply one, two and then three of the dimensions of the rectangular prism by a constant factor (here 5) and calculate the new volume and surface area each time.
The volume of a rectangular prism with dimensions l, b and h is V = l × b × h = lbh.
The surface area of a rectangular prism with dimensions l, b and h is A = 2[(l × h) + (l × b) + (b × h)] = 2(lh + lb + bh).
When one dimension of a rectangular prism (the height) is multiplied by 5, the new volume is V1 = l × b × 5h = 5(lbh) = 5V.
When one dimension of a rectangular prism (the height) is multiplied by 5, the new surface area is A1 = 2[(l × 5h) + (l × b) + (b × 5h)] = 2(5lh + lb + 5bh).
When two dimensions of a rectangular prism (l and h) are multiplied by 5, the new volume is V2 = 5l × b × 5h = 5.5(lbh) = 5^2 × V.
When two dimensions of a rectangular prism (l and h) are multiplied by 5, the new surface area is A2 = 2[(5l × 5h) + (5l × b) + (b × 5h)] = 2 × 5(5lh + lb + bh).
When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by 5, the new volume is V3 = 5l × 5b × 5h = 5^3(lbh) = 5^3 V.
When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by 5, the new surface area is A3 = 2(5^2 lh + 5^2 lb + 5^2 bh) = 5^2 × 2(lh + lb + bh) = 5^2 A.
When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by a factor k, the new volume is V_k = kl × kb × kh = k^3(lbh) = k^3 V; volume is multiplied by k^3.

When all three dimensions of a rectangular prism are multiplied by a factor k, the new surface area is A_k = 2[(kl × kh) + (kl × kb) + (kb × kh)] = k^2 × 2(lh + lb + bh) = k^2 A; surface area is multiplied by k^2.
The new surface area is written A_n and the new volume is written V_n.

To express the new surface area and volume as a factor of the original, first calculate the original volume and surface area, then the new volume and surface area, then compare the new values with the original ones.
Step 1: the original volume of the prism with base lengths 3 cm and height 4 cm is V = l × b × h = 3 × 3 × 4 = 36 cm^3.
Step 1: the original surface area of the prism is A = 2[(l × h) + (l × b) + (b × h)] = 2[(3 × 4) + (3 × 3) + (3 × 4)] = 66 cm^2.
Step 2: multiplying both base lengths by 3 means two of the dimensions are multiplied by a factor of 3.
Step 2: the new volume is V_n = 3l × 3b × h = 3(3) × 3(3) × 4 = 324 cm^3.
Step 3: to express the new volume as a factor of the original, divide V_n by V: V_n / V = 324 / 36 = 9, so V_n = 9V = 3^2 V.
Step 3: to express the new surface area as a factor of the original, divide A_n by A: A_n / A = 306 / 66, so A_n = (306/66)A = (51/11)A.
To prove the effect of multiplying the height by k, write the new dimensions of the prism as l, b and kh.
With the height multiplied by k, the new volume is V_n = l × b × (kh) = k(lbh) = kV.
If the height of a rectangular prism is multiplied by a constant k, then the volume also increases by a factor of k.
In this example the volume of a cylinder with radius r and height h is V = πr^2 × h.
In this example the surface area of the cylinder is given as A = πr^2 + 2πrh.
When the radius of the cylinder is multiplied by k, the new dimensions are kr and h.
When the radius of a cylinder is multiplied by k, the new volume is V_n = π(kr)^2 × h = πk^2 r^2 × h = k^2 × πr^2 h = k^2 V.
When the radius of a cylinder is multiplied by k, the new surface area is A_n = π(kr)^2 + 2π(kr)h = πk^2 r^2 + 2πkrh = k^2(πr^2) + k(2πrh).
